name: Beezaasan Explotech Limited
summary: Explosives manufacturing has genuine operating assets, but recent revenue contraction, weak cash conversion and a large related-party share swap do not support the dated market valuation. Completed financing-linked scenarios remain unattractive even in the favorable case; the illustrative position is smaller than one trading lot.
identity_note: Beezaasan Explotech Limited, BSE544369, ISIN INE13VU01016. Annual report identifies 3 March 2025 listing; official interoperability file supports 800-share lot. March allotment and October voting base establish 15,151,774 actual shares. Proposed October issue is not treated as allotted.

quote.kind: Secondary EquityPandit closing observation, not live or exchange-verified

score_note: BQS 3.62 and GQS 2.85; IAS raw 1.655, final NS under the evidenced reference-position G4 override. All factor inputs are scored and raw arithmetic retained. No persistent CAP/CASH cap is asserted.

gates.reason: Historical statutory board-composition qualification and related-party swap require remediation and capital-allocation monitoring; inspected evidence does not establish severe integrity failure.
Core, minority and associate scopes and major claims are reconciled. Cash classification has an explicit analyst bridge, not corrected audited figures; no unsupported missing-cash allegation.
Reference needs conditional 15.13 crore new credit; no-new-credit path fails. Proposed issue may cover the gap only if actually completed. No existing default is inferred.
At the dated quote an800-share lot costs₹588,040, exceeding the illustrative₹500,000 position. This is a position-size incompatibility, not an exchange suspension finding.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Beezaasan has an operating explosives business, not merely a proposed factory. Nevertheless, FY2026 sales decline while working capital and capital employed rise, and a large related-party share swap introduces valuation risk. Completed linked models give bear/base/bull terminal values₹0.00/₹183.17/₹513.52 against the dated ₹735.05 observation. Even the favorable case has a negative annualized return. This is an unattractive modeled entry, not a claim that industrial operations have no value. [S1] [S6] [S90]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff: 20 October 2026; BSE SME544369, ISIN INE13VU01016. Secondary19 October close₹735.05 and official800-share lot are distinguished from a live executable quote. Consolidated accounts are in crore; target FY2025 statements are in thousands and converted explicitly. Five annual projections end March 2031, while return duration from October 2026 is about 4.447 years. March opening balances are not represented as an October balance sheet. G1/G2/G3 are Conditional; G4 fails only for the illustrative₹5 lakh reference position. [S1] [S9] [S90] [S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 3.62, GQS 2.85, IAS raw 1.655, final NS under G4. All factors have Medium confidence; no historical9–10 or persistent-quality cap. IAS is excluded for the reference-position lot constraint, final NS under the implementation override despite completed calculations. GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 1, DUR 5, CAP 3, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 4 have supporting and contrary evidence. R 1 is the explicit return-spread band; D 1 reflects loss/funding stress; P 1 reflects reverse expectations; L 1 reflects minimum-lot incompatibility rather than a fictitious absence of trades. Point forecasts remain uncertain, but the coarse weak investment bands are robust across modeled sensitivities. A one-point CAP/CASH change alters BQS0.22 and GQS0.25, not the basic conclusion. [S1] [S2] [S90]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company manufactures industrial explosives for mining, quarrying and infrastructure demand, with slurry/emulsion and related initiation products. Licenses, safe manufacture, storage and customer qualification are necessary operating conditions. RHP concentration was material: top 10 customers56.70% and suppliers77.44% in the stated consolidated period; this is not claimed to be the current customer book. Asawara Industries became wholly owned during FY2026; Defence retains a small minority, Safetycord was newly incorporated and not operating, and Asawara Earthtech is an associate rather than a fully consolidated revenue subsidiary. Associate sales are therefore not added to issuer sales. [S1] [S2]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Regulatory and technical requirements provide entry friction, not an automatic economic moat. Raw-material dependence and customer concentration limit pricing freedom. The RHP’s dated FY2024 comparison gives Beezaasan EBITDA margin5.67% versus Premier21.53% and Solar22.56%, but scale, mix and scope differ. This comparison tests competitive economics; it does not supply a current peer median or justify borrowing a large-company valuation multiple. Current customer retention, realized pricing and margin stability would be stronger moat evidence than installed capacity alone. [S2]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated consolidated revenue was₹140.949/227.918/186.3585 crore in FY2022/23/24, then₹214.9951/211.5812 crore in FY2025/26. FY2023–FY2026 CAGR is−2.45%; the four-year FY2022 endpoint is+10.69%, showing why cycle selection matters. Restated financial sales are not silently mixed with higher RHP business/KPI sales. [S1] [S2]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Approved IPO-object changes fund a₹25.7678 crore detonator project; shareholder approval occurred 17 September, not merely a proposal. Fuse commissioning and emulsion/bulk permit delays show mixed execution. The September 2027 detonator target remains a management timetable; model revenue is an assumption, not secured backlog. [S1] [S2] [S8]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The FY2026 secretarial audit reports that the company did not meet the statutory requirement for at least one-third independent directors from 25 November 2025 through 31 March 2026. The board response says corrective steps had been initiated. Completion of that remediation was not verified; this is a dated compliance finding, not a claim that the shortfall necessarily continued at the research cutoff. The RHP also describes historical filing delays and clerical compliance errors, with applications and payments disclosed by the issuer. These findings do not establish diversion, fraud or a current payment default. The2 March 2026 issue of 2,230,641 Beezaasan shares at ₹236 acquired 347,480 of 997,500 Asawara Earthtech shares, about 34.8351%, for₹52.6431 crore noncash consideration. It is not a cash purchase and not an addition of gross target revenue. The target valuation used₹1,515/share and 50/50 market/DCF weighting while NAV received zero weight. Its DCF assumes target sales jumping from ₹9.50 crore to ₹137.33 crore in one year; these are management forecasts, not audited growth. Independent reports and approvals are relevant safeguards but do not prove fair realized returns. [S1] [S2] [S6] [S7]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY2026 owners PAT₹13.2746 crore versus₹13.1229 crore looks stable, but strict operating EBIT falls from ₹20.6675 crore to ₹17.5514 crore after excluding other income; EBITDA falls from ₹23.2882 crore to ₹20.6614 crore. Finance cost declines to ₹1.6625 crore from ₹3.6666 crore. Group PAT before associate₹13.4248 plus associate₹0.0089 less minority₹0.1591 reconciles owners PAT. Statutory weighted EPS 10.13 versus 13.42 is not the same as current-issued profit/share about ₹8.76. Reported CFO₹1.7666 crore minus cash capex₹12.7162 crore gives−₹10.9496 crore before financing-classified interest. Finance-cost addback/interest-income removal suggests analyst CFO about ₹1.98–1.99 crore, still weak. Advance and provision cash-flow differences offset to ₹0.1671 crore, matching tax paid less current tax expense; one leg is not labeled missing cash. These are classification bridges, not corrected audited statements. [S1] Operating WC rises from ₹35.5284 crore to ₹50.2243 crore. Capital employed including liquid funds but excluding the nonoperating associate rises from ₹121.2539 crore to ₹139.6478 crore; normalized operating return is about 10.07%, and the latest incremental return is negative. Cash-excluded return is about 12%, so capital-definition sensitivity is explicit. Reported debt₹37.0399 crore includes₹0.1746 crore nonrepayable subsidy, leaving financial debt₹36.8653 crore. Deposit release₹21.5685 crore is modeled alongside mandatory settlement of ₹18.0867 crore collateral OD, not as free cash while leaving secured debt untouched. Current tax₹0.6957 crore and net current benefits₹0.0533 crore settle once; salary, expenses, statutory and CSR provisions already sit in WC. Gross gratuity₹0.3356 less plan assets₹0.2563 equals net₹0.0793, split current₹0.0238 and noncurrent₹0.0555. Net NC benefits₹0.2619 and DTL₹2.3491 remain terminal claims; future service costs remain in operating margins. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The reference uses actual 1.5151774 crore shares, no unreceived issue proceeds, core growth 0/3/5/5/5%, project sales 0/8/25/40/50 crore, core/project EBITDA margins 9.5%/16%, WC 26%/35%, maintenance 2% of core revenue, 10% debt cost and 10× exit EBIT. New project cash capex excludes opening CWIP₹2.9993 crore from the₹25.7678 crore budget. Unknown-purpose capital advance₹6.1625 crore is retained separately; a same-project sensitivity applies it once and removes the terminal asset. Interest includes half-year new draws. Reference required new borrowing is₹15.13 crore and is not committed credit. Base terminal₹183.17 gives-26.84% annualized; bear equity is zero and bull₹513.52 gives-7.75%. No-credit base fails. Associate value is a separate net-equity/retained-ROE bridge, not the optimistic valuer DCF or a second addition of its₹52.652 crore carrying cost. No dividends or target cash sweep are assumed. [S1] [S4] [S6] [S9] [S90] The positive variant is that permits, product mix and associate resources yield far more earnings than recent history. Target FY2025 audited sales₹14.7406 crore/PAT₹0.2176 crore/CFO−₹1.7974 crore and FY2026 AOC sales₹8.9192 crore/PAT₹0.546 crore do not yet establish the valuer’s scaling case. Target FY2026 net assets₹11.4208 crore already deduct reported liabilities; no unverified debt-free claim is made. Base terminal sensitivities include about ₹199.51 if the approved issue completes with paired cash/shares/fees,₹215.24 if the full associate carrying value is recoverable,₹124.79 at 7% core margin, and₹163.01 at 35% WC. Even these do not approach entry. A 15% return at ₹735.05 requires roughly 65.49% annual core growth,₹2,676.60 crore terminal sales and₹411.50 crore conditional borrowing under the other base assumptions. Fivefold/tenfold price outcomes require approximately 103.15%/133.99% growth and much larger funding. These reverse cases expose expectations, not forecasts or automatic impossibility claims. [S1] [S6] [S9] [S90]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The bear combines a 10% initial core-sales decline, 6% core EBITDA margin, 35% operating WC, delayed project sales, 25% project overrun, 13% financing cost and 7× exit EBIT. Opening raw-material/receivable impairments reduce realizable WC once; replacement funding then reflects the lower opening asset base. Noncore assets recover only 50%, with no double cash impairment charge. The path needs about ₹76.10 crore conditional new borrowing and terminal financial claims exhaust equity. Denying new credit causes an earlier liquidity-floor failure, not a valid computed terminal return. Even the reference fails without replacement credit, so the key thesis-break variables are actual financing access, permits and collections. Assets and possible equity issuance are counterweights, not guaranteed rescue. [S1] [S4]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At the dated entry, fivefold and tenfold terminal prices require about 103.15% and 133.99% annual core growth under otherwise unchanged reference economics, with terminal sales about ₹7,371.35 crore/₹14,891.75 crore and conditional additional debt about ₹1,306.63 crore/₹2,784.20 crore. Required cumulative cash capex is about ₹302.81 crore/₹533.75 crore. These are linked reverse calculations, not a market-size claim or feasible financing commitment. Recent contracting sales and weak cash conversion do not support either outcome. [S1] [S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track permits, commissioning, project cash spend and customer orders against the September 2027 target. Reconcile deposit collateral release, OD settlement and sanctioned replacement credit before relying on the base funding path. Verify actual allotment, fees and use of the₹29.285 crore proposed issue; October approval is not receipt of cash. September 30 secondary coverage says a further Asawara valuation was requested, not that an additional acquisition closed. Obtain full current target accounts and final transaction terms before expanding the perimeter. Verify independent-director remediation, subsequent regulatory/court status and current RPT terms. Track inventory ageing, collections, operating cash and per-share earnings rather than capacity announcements. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S8] [S10] [S11]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed full-model review with weak assessed quality and unattractive conditional investment economics. Not a buy or compounder classification. A financing route or shareholder-approved transaction does not by itself establish shareholder value. The₹5 lakh reference position cannot buy one 800-share lot at the dated quote. Sixty-session lower-turnover proxy gives roughly 1.96 days at 5% participation, but this is not implementable at that position size; 20-session median gives about 2.09 days. At2%/10%, the 60-session conditional calculation is about 4.89/0.98 days. Missing2 September data are not proof of an actual zero-trade day, and historical turnover does not establish live depth. Reassess only with a feasible position, refreshed market evidence and materially better supported operating/valuation economics. [S90] [S91]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual, RHP, voting and valuation passages were read selectively, not certified cover to cover. Decisive scanned target balance-sheet/P&L tables were visually checked. Two later BSE attachments returned HTTP403; secondary reproductions support a limited chronology, not full primary verification. The issuer second-corrigendum link led to an unrelated older document and was not treated as evidence. Current target claim detail, future permit timing, credit commitments, deposit release terms and independent-director remediation remain unverified. Models explicitly carry existing claims and use conditional financing; no hidden rescue or free acquisition cash is inserted. Market prices are dated secondary observations, and BSE surveillance/spread/depth are not cleared by NSE master fields. [S1] [S2] [S6] [S9] [S10] [S11] [S12] [S13] [S90] [S91]

financial_history.normalization: RHP business/KPI sales differ from restated financial sales. Recent current-issued per-share profit is an analytical denominator, not a restatement of statutory weighted EPS. Associate revenue is not consolidated gross revenue.

GOV.reason: Historical board-composition qualification, filing weaknesses and a large promoter-group share swap warrant 4. Contrary: transaction approvals and valuation reports exist, statutory financial opinion is unmodified, and no diversion is established. The issue is stewardship and valuation discipline, not an invented fraud finding.

MOAT.reason: Licensed explosives production and customer qualification create entry friction. Contrary: customer/supplier concentration, raw-material exposure and much lower dated margins than larger peers do not establish durable pricing power. Existing industrial capability supports 4 rather than NS.

REV.reason: Comparable FY2023–FY2026 restated revenue CAGR is negative2.45%, anchoring 1. FY2026 also contracts1.59%. Contrary: the four-year FY2022 endpoint grows10.69%; this cyclical recovery does not erase recent stagnation. Proposed capacity and associate forecasts are not demonstrated revenue.

DUR.reason: Mining/infrastructure demand and approved detonator investment provide a real expansion route. Contrary: licenses, commissioning and customer absorption remain uncertain; project revenue is modeled, not contracted backlog. Accessible but constrained runway supports5.

CAP.reason: Normalized all-funds capital return about 10.07% and negative recent incremental return support 3; equity and working capital expand while strict EBIT contracts. Contrary: cash-excluded return is about 12% and unfinished assets can mature. One recent cohort does not establish a persistent CAP override.

CASH.reason: Reported CFO is only 13.2% of pre-associate group PAT and pre-interest FCF is negative10.9496 crore. Classification normalization does not cure weak conversion. Contrary: FY2024 CFO 10.0343 was strong; do not assert persistent cash destruction or automatically cap GQS.

BAL.reason: Deposits and equity cushion financial debt, but pledged cash cannot fund the same project and settle OD twice. Base requires15.13 crore conditional new borrowing and fails without it; no allotment proceeds are assumed. Contrary: a completed proposed issue could fund the reference path and there is no evidenced existing payment default.

EXEC.reason: Existing operations and completed share allotment show execution capacity; IPO object revision received shareholder approval. Contrary: delayed permits, changed capital uses and unproven detonator/associate outcomes constrain confidence. Approvals are not earned project returns.

EARN.reason: Owners PAT grows only slightly while strict operating EBIT falls about15.1%; lower finance cost and attribution matter. Contrary: core EBIT remains positive and earnings are not entirely nonoperating. Current-share profit and weighted EPS are separated.

R.reason: Supported conditional base return is −26.84% versus15% hurdle, a −41.84 percentage-point spread and R 1. Favorable return is still negative 7.75%; the low band is robust to modeled asset and financing sensitivities. No-credit failure is not assigned a fictitious positive IRR.

D.reason: Bear equity is exhausted despite conditional additional credit; base without new credit fails its liquidity floor. Contrary: funded assets, existing industrial cash generation and a possible issue offer recovery routes, but not strong shareholder downside support at ₹735.05.

P.reason: At the dated quote, the base 15% hurdle requires about 65.49% annual core growth and more than₹411 crore conditional new debt under otherwise unchanged assumptions. Even recovery of full associate carrying value leaves terminal value far below entry. Price-implied expectations are extreme, independently of the R return-level score.

L.reason: Turnover proxy alone indicates roughly 1.96 days at5% participation, initially band 9. The official800-share lot costs₹588,040, exceeding the₹5 lakh reference position; implementation is infeasible at that reference and L 1/G4 exclusion overrides turnover arithmetic. A larger position requires fresh sizing, spread, circuits and depth checks.

Q.reason: Exact unrounded BQS reused once in IAS.
